comments.author: runeks
comments.story_title: Ubuntu will switch from X window server to Mir
comments.why_zh: 解释了 X 设计上的问题。
comments.quote_zh: 这个视频很好地解释了 X 的一些问题
comments.text_zh: 这个视频很好地解释了 X 的一些问题：[VIDEO] 长话短说：X11 协议（Xorg/X 是它的一个实现）创建于 1980 年，当时是为了绘制像这样的东西：[LINK] X 与任何现代显示服务器之间的重要区别在于，如今我们把合成器（将应用程序内容合成成你在显示器上看到的东西）和工具包（绘制文本框、按钮、进度条等）分成了两部分。X 的设计初衷是同时做这两件事。由于若干原因，这并不实际。到目前为止人们一直在绕过这个问题，但许多人觉得是时候停止绕行了（因为这种“绕行”让 X 的代码库变成了一团乱麻），并从零开始开发一个能满足 2013 年现代桌面需求的东西。
comments.text: Here's a good video explaining some of X's problems: [VIDEO] Long story short: the X11 protocol (which Xorg/X is an implementation of) was created in 1980, and was made for drawing stuff like this: [LINK] The important distinction between X and any modern display server is that nowadays we separate compositor (that which composites application content into what you see on the display) and toolkit (that which draws text boxes, buttons, progress bars etc.) into two. X was designed to do both these things. This isn't practical for several reasons. So far people have worked around this issue, but many feel it's time to stop working around it (since the X codebase is a complete mess due to this "working around"), and develop something from scratch that does what we want for a modern desktop in 2013.

comments.author: forgottenpass
comments.story_title: Xwayland
comments.why_zh: 关于抛弃 X 和 Wayland 是什么的更好解释。
comments.quote_zh: 关于抛弃 X 以及 Wayland 是什么的更好解释：看这个演讲
comments.text_zh: 这属于一个更大的构想：彻底摆脱 X11。不可避免的替代品是 Wayland。* 这种切换的挑战之一在于，一旦你开始用 wayland，你会有一些无法与 wayland 通信的老应用，你得启动一个 X server 来跑那个老应用。如果你的电脑上是 wayland 会话，你不会想按 ctrl-alt-8 切到跑那单个应用的 X 会话，然后再切回 wayland 去用其他每个程序。如果有一个作为 wayland client 工作的 X server，能把只支持 X 的应用放到你的 wayland 桌面上，那就好了。那就是 Xwayland。* 关于抛弃 X 以及 Wayland 是什么的更好解释：看这个来自一位参与 Wayland 的 X 开发者的演讲 [VIDEO]
comments.text: The larger idea this fits into is getting rid of X11 all together. The inevitable replacement is Wayland.* One of the challenges of such a switch will that once you start using wayland, you'll have some older applications that cant talk to wayland, you'd have to start an X server to run that old application. If you have a wayland session on your computer, you don't want to hit ctrl-alt-8 to switch over to an X session running that single application, and then switch back and forth to wayland to use every other program. It would be nice if there was a X server that worked as a wayland client and could put the X-only application on your wayland desktop. That's Xwayland. * For a better explanation on ditching X, and what Wayland is: see this talk from one of the X dudes working on Wayland [VIDEO]

comments.author: lomnakkus
comments.story_title: Fedora 25: With Wayland, Linux has never been easier (or more handsome)
comments.why_zh: 展示 Wayland 清除掉的过时 X11 垃圾。
comments.quote_zh: 如果你想知道到底清掉了哪些垃圾，看看 Daniel Stone 的演讲[2]。
comments.text_zh: 不。就如今 X11 实际被用到的那些部分而言，它基本上已经功能完备了[1]。X11 被一些荒谬过时的扩展拖累，比如画点线、font server 之类。如果你想知道到底清掉了哪些垃圾，看看 Daniel Stone 的演讲[2]。那基本上就是我们在任何类型的 server 进程里都永远不会再想要的东西。带宽和延迟之间的权衡在计算的几乎所有领域都发生了根本变化，尤其是任何与图形有关的部分。[1] 好吧，可能还缺一些零碎东西，但正如正在讨论的这篇文章所见证的，没什么大不了的。[2] [VIDEO]
comments.text: No. It's already basically feature-complete as compared to which parts of X11 are actually used these days[1]. X11 is burdened by absurdly obsolete extensions like drawing stippled lines, a font server, etc. See the talk by Daniel Stone[2] if you're interested in the kind of crud that's been cleared out. It's basically the kind of stuff that we will never go back to wanting in any type of server process. The trade-off between bandwidth and latency has changed fundamentally in basically all areas of computing, but especially anything to do with graphics. [1] Alright, there might be a few bits and bobs that are missing, but nothing major as witnessed by the very article under discussion. [2] [VIDEO]

comments.text: "X isn't network transparent anymore" according to Daniel Stone (longtime X.org and Wayland developer): [VIDEO] If you use X11 forwarding with any application that uses a modern toolkit (Gtk+ 3, Qt 5, maybe also Gtk+ 2 and Qt 4) you are just pushing uncompressed pixmaps over the wire, as a bad substitute for VNC/RDP/etc. Xpra adds image compression on top, AFAIK, so it should be slightly better. The entire video ( [VIDEO] ) provides a good overview as to why people that have been working on X11 for many many years decided to start Wayland.

我同意 Wayland 的开发拖得太久，过渡也很坎坷。但哪个开发团队不想要更多资金呢？Ubuntu 在生态系统拒绝 Mir 后闹脾气，又不为 Wayland 做贡献，这当然没有帮助。

我对 Red Hat 也有意见，但我的观点是：Wayland 是由 Xorg 开发者创造的，因为他们尝试让 X11 保持竞争力却失败了。说真的，去看看这位 XFree86/Xorg/Wayland 开发者的演讲[1]。

[1]: [视频]
comments.text: > Screenshots/recording should have been on the board from day one and they could have gotten to standardizing on how to handle them in oh 2013-2015? I agree that Wayland's development has taken far too long and the transition has been rocky. But what development team couldn't use more funding? Ubuntu throwing a tantrum after the ecosystem rejected Mir and not contributing to Wayland certainly didn't help. > What other OS makes you think about display servers? I am sympathetic to arguments that Wayland/Weston could provide more functionality out-of-the-box. The bazaar's fragmented mess of "desktop environments" is certainly not a strength compared to what the Cathedrals have produced. But Linux's uniquely modular GUI stack necessitates coordination across lots of projects to develop and adopt standards. But not doing anything and sticking with X11 would have condemned us to being stuck with an insecure, buggy, and visually glitchy mess forever. > Red Hat doesn't believe in the Linux ecosystem I have my qualms with Red Hat too, but my point was that Wayland was created by Xorg developers because they tried and failed to make X11 competitive. Seriously, just go watch this XFree86/Xorg/Wayland developer's talk [1]. [1]: [VIDEO]

comments.author: slacka
comments.story_title: Ubuntu: One OS, one interface, all devices
comments.why_zh: 被引用来支持对 X 的批评。
comments.text_zh: 首先，手机模式和桌面模式下的 UI 并不一样。桌面模式下运行的是传统 Unity，移动模式下运行的是 Ubuntu Touch，这是一种基于手势的 UI，只是看起来和 Unity 相似。我在 BlackBerry 10 上用过一段时间，我很喜欢。基于手势的 UI 是智能手机的未来。在 Unity 和 Mir 这件事上，我愿意对 Ubuntu 宽容一些。尽管有一堆黑子，最新的 Unity 其实正在变成一个相当不错的 UI。对我们这些用 16:9 显示器的人来说，垂直任务栏是正确的选择。垂直任务栏在 GNOME[1] 里坏了十多年，所以我能理解 Shuttleworth 的沮丧。我也很喜欢搜索栏 lens UI。他们犯的错误是半成品就把 Unity 发布了。是的，在低端硬件上它可能会变得卡顿无响应。但这很大程度上来自 Linux 下糟糕的 3D 驱动支持，以及臃肿、缓慢、过时的 X[2] 和 compiz。这两者死得越早，我们就能越早在 Linux 下拥有响应灵敏的现代 3D 加速合成窗口管理器。[1] [LINK] [2] [VIDEO]
comments.text: First of all, the UI is not the same when in phone mode and desktop mode. In desktop mode it runs traditional Unity and in mobile mode it runs Ubuntu Touch, a gesture based UI that only looks similar to Unity. I spent some time on a BlackBerry 10, and I loved it. Gesture based UIs are the future for smartphones. I'm willing to cut Ubuntu some slack on Unity and Mir. Despite all the haters, the latest Unity is actually turning out to be a decent UI. For those of us on 16:9 monitors, a vertical taskbar was the right choice. Vertical taskbars were broken for over 10 years GNOME[1], so I can understand Shuttleworths frustration. I also love the search bar lense UI. The mistake they made was shipping Unity half-baked. Yes, it can get unresponsive on low-end hardware. But much of this comes from poor 3D driver support under Linux, and bloated, slow, and outdated X[2] and compiz. The sooner those two die, the sooner we can have a responsive modern 3D accelerated compositing window managers under Linux. [1] [LINK] [2] [VIDEO]

comments.why_zh: X 臃肿又浪费这一说法的来源。

comments.text_zh: 据知情人士[1]说，X 在 CPU 占用、接口复杂度和无用代码方面都严重臃肿。X 花大量时间做无用功，比如即使知道屏幕那部分会被有用的东西重写，它还是要画一个灰色矩形。完全转向 Wayland 肯定会让系统更轻。但传统的 X 客户端运行在 XWayland 里。我不知道 XWayland 除了兼容性之外还提供了什么，但往后，随着越来越多的工具包和窗口管理器脱离 X，“较弱”的电脑会有更多资源去做有用的事。[1] [VIDEO]
comments.text: According to people in the know[1], X is severely bloated in terms of CPU usage, interface complexity, and useless code. X spends a lot of time performing useless actions, such as drawing a gray rectangle even when it knows that part of the screen is going to be rewritten by something useful. Going full-Wayland is bound to be lighter on the system. But traditional X clients run within XWayland. I don't know if XWayland offers anything more than compatibility, but going forward, as more and more toolkits and window managers wean themselves off X, "weaker" computers will have more resources to spend on doing useful stuff. [1] [VIDEO]

comments.author: kevincox
comments.story_title: Fedora 40 Eyes Dropping Gnome X11 Session Support
comments.why_zh: 引用它来说明 Core X11 已退化为低效的 IPC。
comments.quote_zh: X11 架构曾是网络透明的绘图原语。
comments.text_zh: 问题在于，X11 架构已经死了十年。X11 架构曾是网络透明的绘图原语。现代 X 的几乎所有功能都是通过扩展完成的。你的绘图是用 OpenGL 或类似接口完成的，缓冲区通过共享内存传递，大量显示元数据和配置也是通过扩展完成的。实际渲染由窗口管理器完成（假设你在做合成）。正如 Daniel Stone 所说，"Core X11" 剩下的只是非常糟糕的 IPC。（因为客户端与 X 通信，X 与窗口管理器通信，窗口管理器再与 X 通信，X 再与客户端通信，每个请求需要两次往返）[VIDEO] 所以拯救 Core X11 是死路一条。你剩下的只是一个带有不必要往返的基础 IPC 系统。因此，剩下能拯救的只有扩展。你可以保留 GLX 和 Vulkan 的对应部分，但把它们从 IPC 中剥离后，剩下的也不多了。所以真的，不行。那些能被拯救的东西太基础了（比如传递输入事件），不如直接用更好的 IPC 协议重新实现它们。对于需要向后兼容的客户端，还有 XWayland（尽管出于安全原因它受限）。
comments.text: The problem is that the X11 architecture has been dead for a decade. The X11 architecture was network-transparent drawing primitives. Almost all of modern X is done via extensions. Your drawing is done using OpenGL or some similar interface, buffers are passed using shared memory, lots of display metadata and configuration is done via extensions as well. The actual rendering is done by the window manager (assuming you are doing compositing). As Daniel Stone said, all that is left of "Core X11" is really bad IPC. (As the client talks to X which talks to the window manager which talks to X which talks to the client, requiring 2 round-trips for every request) [VIDEO] So saving Core X11 is a dead end. All you have is a basic IPC system with unnecessary round-trips. So all that is left to save is the extensions. You can save GLX and the Vulkan equivalent but tearing them from the IPC is leaving not much behind. So really, no. The things that could be saved are so basic (like feeding input events) that it is better to just re-implement them using a better IPC protocol. For clients that need backwards compatibility there is XWayland (although it is limited for security reasons).
